text: Is the matrix A = [[3, 1], [0, 3]] diagonalizable over ℝ?
choices: No — the eigenvalue 3 has algebraic multiplicity 2 but geometric multiplicity 1
Yes — it is already upper triangular
Yes — its characteristic polynomial has the double root 3
No — it has no real eigenvalues
explanation: A − 3I = [[0,1],[0,0]] has a one-dimensional kernel, span{e₁}, so there is no basis of eigenvectors. A diagonalizable matrix with only eigenvalue 3 would have to equal 3I.
